artworks.title: Hippolytus, Phaedra and the Nurse
artworks.description: Herculaneum fresco: lovesick Phaedra and her nurse opposite the chaste Hippolytus — Euripides' confession scene on a Campanian wall.

artworks.title: Hippolytus after the Confession of Phaedra, his Stepmother
artworks.description: Garnier's Salon canvas — Hippolytus recoiling after Phaedra's confession, the instant that sets Theseus' curse in motion.

artworks.title: The Death of Hippolytus (La mort d'Hippolyte)
artworks.description: Lemoyne's Louvre marble — Poseidon's sea-bull panics the horses and Hippolytus is dragged in the reins, Euripides' catastrophe in stone.

artworks.title: The Death of Hippolytus
artworks.description: Alma-Tadema's shore: the bull surges from the waves as the chariot wrecks — the chaste hunter destroyed by a father's curse.

films.title: Phaedra
films.description: Dassin's modern Greece retelling — Melina Mercouri's Phaedra destroying her stepson — keeps Euripides on screen.

popCulture.title: Hippolytus (play)
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' tragedy of the chaste hunter and the stepmother's desire — still the source text for every Phaedra.

popCulture.title: Phèdre
popCulture.creator: Jean Racine
popCulture.description: Racine's French classic remakes Hippolytus' doom for the neoclassical stage — passion as fatal clarity.
